# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** In the histories of the twelve tribes of Israel it is written: There was a certain Joachim, exceedingly rich, and he brought his gifts double before the Lord God, saying within himself, "The abundance which is for all the people shall be mine; and my gift shall be for the forgiveness of all the people, and my repentance before the Lord God shall be for my atonement."

**1:2** And the great day of the Lord drew near, and the sons of Israel were bringing their gifts. And Reuben stood before him and said, "It is not lawful for you to bring your gifts first, because you have not made seed in Israel."

**1:3** And Joachim was exceedingly grieved, and he went away to the records of the twelve tribes of the people, saying, "I will search the records of the twelve tribes of Israel to see whether I alone have not made seed in Israel." And he searched and found that all the righteous had raised up seed in Israel. And he remembered the patriarch Abraham, that in his last days God gave him a son, Isaac.

**1:4** And Joachim was exceedingly grieved, and he did not appear to his wife but went into the wilderness, and he pitched his tent there and fasted forty days and forty nights, saying within himself, "I will not go down either for food or for drink until the Lord my God shall visit me; prayer shall be my food and drink."
